sn52.8:1.1: _Salaḷa_ is usually identified with frankincense (variant _sallakī_, Sanskrit _śallakī_, *Boswellia serrata*), but this is uncertain. Frankincense thrives in arid highlands quite distant from the rich riverlands of Sāvatthī, and is a straggly tree unsuited to construction (although the hut could simply be near a frankincense). The Apadāna refers to flowers or garlands of _salaḷa_ ([tha-ap209](), [tha-ap212:11.4](), [tha-ap556:3.3)), but the frankincense flower is small and a poor candidate for garlands. [mn93:11.6]() and [mn96:16.3]() speak of the fire from the _salaḷa_. No Pali reference, so far as I know, speaks of the most characteristic feature of frakincense, its aromatic gum. Perhaps there is a confusion with the pine tree _sarala_ (*Pinus roxburghii*).
